correctness.rationale: Exactly enumerated tournament directed chain groups have dimensions 11,55,110,55; signed boundary ranks are rank(∂₂)=45 and rank(∂₃)=55, with integer Smith factors of ∂₃ equal to 54 ones and one two. Exactly 55 of all 462 induced five-vertex complexes contain six-face oriented two-spheres and form a free orbit under 55 affine symmetries. Each chosen six-triangle signed fundamental cycle is explicitly verified to be closed. The joined matrix of the 55 three-boundary columns and 55 carrier cycle columns has 65 nonzero Smith factors, all ones. As all these columns lie in the primitive rank-65 kernel of ∂₂, this proves integral equality and hence entire H₂ generation. Half of the sum of all tetrahedron boundaries is integral and of order two, nonzero by rational injectivity of ∂₃, and fixed under affine permutation of unique transitive orders. The package verifier reconstructs and repeats all nonstandard rank, Smith and enumeration computations from its source.

originality.rationale: Govc (2020, Proposition 3.4) already determines the order-eleven doubly regular tournament Moore-space homotopy type and hence its abstract degree-two torsion; no novelty is asserted for that. The new exact geometric claims classify 55 inclusion-minimal induced five-vertex sphere carriers and prove their images generate the entire integral homology lattice, including torsion, with a concrete invariant half-boundary cycle. Full relevant sections of Govc and Masulli–Villa were inspected and targeted indexed research comparisons did not provide an equivalent support/lattice result. Bibliographic priority beyond those inspections is not certified.
residual_risks: Equivalent unpublished or unindexed lists of tournament induced subcomplexes or a computational notebook could contain the same support/lattice theorem; absolute priority is not established.

value.rationale: The canonical eleven-vertex doubly regular tournament is the first order with a Moore-space torsion summand in its directed flag homotopy classification. Identifying exact shortest vertex carriers and showing they collectively generate not only the free part but the global order-two torsion is a local-to-global structural theorem that abstract homotopy classification does not imply. The affine-invariant signed tetrahedron half-boundary explains that torsion geometrically. The five-vertex support cutoff and orbit of 55 carriers are natural and fully classified rather than an arbitrarily chosen small slice.
